newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs shed gains but tone still firm.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs shed gains but tone still firm.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen and Japanese government bond (JGB) futures subsided in late Thursday trade after touching new contract highs early in the day on continuing signs of weakness in Japan's economy.

Dealers attributed the late slippage to profit-taking and a knee-jerk reaction to comments by an ex-Ministry of Finance (MOF) official but said the fundamental view that Japan's economy could not yet sustain a rate rise remained intact.
Tomomitsu Oba, former vice minister of international affairs, said now was not the time for Japan to change its monetary policy.
"The market must have been overtraded since yesterday. This is a healthy correction. It'll give people a chance to go long," a senior dealer at an Asian institution said.

He said the lead March Euroyen contract should remain supported at 99.15 for the time being. It stood at 99.17 at 1200 GMT after hitting a high of 99.22 against an IMM close at 99.19. Dealers said the market opened firm after Wednesday's sharp gains on weaker than expected June industrial output data.

News that a major Japanese construction firm had filed for court protection under bankruptcy laws and Yamaichi Securities' disclosure of its links with racketeers on Wednesday also contributed to the market's firm bias.
A trader at a U.S. futures house said a 6.5 percent year-on-year drop in Japan's June construction orders provided further support.
"The construction numbers were rather supportive of the market because they point to continued easy monetary policy," the trader said.
September JGBs ended at 126.37 against a previous 126.38 after failing to breach a topside of 122.55.
Eurodollar futures ended steady but well underpinned as players adjusted their positions ahead of the release of the U.S. second quarter gross domestic product, due at 1230 GMT.
"Sentiment is that the economy is doing well and there's not much fear of inflation," the trader said, adding that December Eurodollars could breach resistance at 94.20 and head for 94.25.
The contract ended unchanged from its IMM close, at 94.185.
